key_insight: Interfaces between dissimilar 2D materials generate out-of-plane dipoles that can be tuned by in-plane strain, enabling interface-engineered electromechanical coupling.
engineering_relevance: Work-function mismatch and interfacial charge redistribution offer design guides for strain-tunable electromechanical components based on van der Waals heterostructures.
method: Screened 461 heterostructures assembled from 57 monolayers using high-throughput DFT.
Linked work-function mismatch, charge redistribution, and interfacial dipoles under biaxial strain.
Compared charge-density-difference and Berry-phase calculations for semiconducting heterostructures.
evidence_signal: Among 24 selected heterostructures, effective biaxial interfacial electromechanical coefficients reached 83.35 pC/m; the two calculation methods agreed within 10% for semiconducting systems.
watch_item: Results are computational; metallic interfaces show strain-tunable dipoles rather than the well-defined piezoelectric response identified in semiconducting systems.
paper_title: Interface-Engineered Piezoelectricity and Electromechanical Coupling in Two-Dimensional van der Waals Heterostructures
